requirement: Requirement and reference names MUST have nonempty dot-separated segments containing only ASCII letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens. A `{req}` directive whose full name is invalid, including one whose chapter path gives an invalid namespace, and a role with an invalid name MUST remain literal and MUST NOT define or reference a requirement. For nested chapter paths, a leading `reqs/` and a final `index` or `README` segment MUST be omitted from the requirement namespace.
rationale:
`requirements.ci.identifiers` is met. I found no gap in the code or the tests.

**Obligations and the code that carries them out**
- **Valid names.** Names need nonempty dot-separated segments of ASCII letters, digits, `_` or `-`. `src/lib.rs#fn[valid_name]` checks exactly that.
- **Invalid `{req}` full names stay literal and define nothing.**
  - `src/evidence.rs#fn[collect_definitions]` builds the full name with `full_requirement_name`, reports an invalid one as an error, and does not insert it. This includes a name that is invalid because the chapter path gives an invalid namespace.
  - `src/lib.rs#fn[preprocess_book]` skips such names when it builds its definitions map.
  - `src/lib.rs#fn[replace_definitions]` renders only blocks whose full name is valid, so the others stay literal.
  - `src/lib.rs#fn[definition_blocks]` ignores a block whose local name is invalid, unless it is a built-in name.
- **Roles with invalid names stay literal and reference nothing.**
  - Inline roles: `src/lib.rs#fn[reference_roles]` returns only roles whose name passes `valid_name` or is a built-in name. `preprocess_book` reaches it through `replace_references` and `replace_inline_references`.
  - Fenced roles: `src/fenced.rs#fn[opening_fence]` applies the same check. `preprocess_book` reaches it through `replace_references`, `markdown_fences` and `find_fences`.
- **Namespace from nested chapter paths.** `src/lib.rs#fn[chapter_namespace]` drops a leading `reqs/` and a final `index` or `README` segment. It does so only when the path has more than one component. Both `collect_definitions` and `preprocess_book` use it.

All of this code is reachable from the two `{impl}` items, `collect_definitions` and `preprocess_book`, so it needs no references of its own.

**Tests**
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[invalid_names_remain_literal]` covers:
  - empty segments, spaces, non-ASCII `é`, `/`, `&` and backticks;
  - valid names with `_`, `-` and digits;
  - invalid names in all four inline roles, in both markdown and non-markdown modes;
  - invalid names after `{req}`, `{example}` and `{definition}`;
  - a valid local name in a chapter with an invalid namespace staying literal.
- `src/fenced.rs#mod[tests]/fn[opening_fences_take_a_role_and_one_valid_or_built_in_name]` covers invalid names in fenced roles.
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[chapter_path_prefixes_the_requirement_name]` covers the `reqs/`, `index` and `README` omissions. It also covers the cases where nothing is dropped (`index.md`, `reqs.md`, `other/reqs/a.md`).
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[chapters_with_invalid_namespaces_define_nothing_in_the_book]` runs `preprocess_book`. It checks that the invalid-namespace chapter and a reference to it both stay literal.
- `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[invalid_full_names_from_chapter_paths_are_reported_and_not_defined]` runs `collect_definitions` through `validate_repository`. It checks that an invalid full name is not defined and that `reqs/index.md` gets an empty namespace.
- `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[validates_full_names_requirement_text_and_input_lines]` and `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[examples_are_distinct_definitions_and_tests_link_to_them]` also carry `{test}` references to the requirement.

The extra errors that `collect_definitions` emits (invalid name, `habeas:` reserved names) fall under `requirements.ci.errors` and `requirements.references.builtin_definitions`. The same code marks both with `{impl}`, so they are specified behavior.
